chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: The valve trombone that was really an alto horn
summary: Willard corrects a Down Beat story: he bought a trombone-shaped alto horn hanging in a Milwaukee butcher shop and kept it until the Army.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Tell that story about how the Down Beat and other places reported you playing the valve trombone on the Ken Club---

Well, I got it in Milwaukee once - I bought this thing-- I was with a guy to a butcher shop and he was buying some meat for dinner and hanging on one of the hooks in this butcher shop there was this old, beat-up - it looked like a trombone, but it wasn't. When I got it - he said - you want to see it - it's been hanging up there since we owned this place. And, it was black - it had been hanging there so long and I looked at it and it was an alto--
Yeah - that's what I was going to say -- I said you played the valve trombone and you said, I did - you didn't. What you really played was this---
It was actually an alto horn---

It looked exactly like a trombone. And, the guy sold me that horn for $10.00 or something or $15.00 or $5.00 -- it was so cheap and once I cleaned it up it was beautiful and it had a lovely sound and I had that until I went in the Army.
Does the picture of you look like you're playing a trombone, but it's this -- what you call - an alto horn---
Well, it absolutely is a trombone - a valve trombone-to look at it you'd swear it was a valve trombone, but it was a little smaller
